intro: People kicked and carried balls for hundreds of years before anyone wrote a rule book. English towns played rough folk games in their streets. American college students argued over rules before each game. In this unit you will see how those games became two sports with written codes: American football and soccer.

Each sport got its shape from people who met and wrote things down. Walter Camp and the college rules meetings made the gridiron. The Football Association, IFAB and FIFA made a pitch the whole world could share. Injuries, bans and new laws changed who could play and how safely.

You will be able to put key dates in order and name who made each rule. You will explain how a school field and a world stadium are public places. You will also tell when women and girls were shut out of soccer, and when doors opened again.
bigQuestion: How did two kinds of football grow from rough local games into written codes played on school fields and world stadiums?

test.q: Which game from 1869 is often called the first college football game?
What did Walter Camp's 1880 rule set?
choices: eleven players a side and a line of scrimmage
test.why: In 1880 the colleges accepted eleven a side and the line of scrimmage.

test.q: Why is a football field called a gridiron?
choices: it was first made of iron
Walter Camp lived on Gridiron Street
its chalk lines made it look like a grill
test.why: Lines every five yards made the field look like a cooking grill.

test.q: What happened after many injuries and deaths in college football?
choices: new rules in 1906, including the forward pass
test.why: The 1905 crisis led to the 1906 rule changes.

test.q: What does Memorial Stadium in Champaign honor?
choices: Illinois people who died in World War I
test.why: Its columns carry the names of Illinois people who died in World War I.
Boys soccer began in 1972, before football in 1974, girls soccer in 1988 and the Fire in 1997.

test.q: What was banned in London in 1314?
test.why: A 1314 proclamation under Edward II banned football in London.

test.q: Who drafted the FA's first laws in 1863?
test.why: Morley, the FA's first secretary, drafted its laws.

test.q: Which two things did the FA's 1863 laws ban?
test.why: The 1863 laws banned carrying the ball and hacking.

test.q: Which group decides changes to soccer's Laws of the Game?
test.why: IFAB, formed in 1886, decides changes to the Laws.

test.q: How many countries' associations founded FIFA in 1904?
test.why: Seven European associations founded FIFA in Paris.

test.q: Which country won the first World Cup?
test.why: Uruguay beat Argentina 4 to 2 in Montevideo in 1930.

test.q: What did the FA do in 1971?
choices: lifted its ban on women's teams
test.why: In 1971 the FA lifted the 1921 ban on women's teams.

test.q: How is a conference different from a federation like FIFA?
choices: a conference writes the Laws of the Game
a federation is a single school
a conference is a group of schools; FIFA joins national associations
test.why: A conference groups schools; FIFA is a federation of national associations.

test.q: Where did the 1994 World Cup open?
test.why: Germany played Bolivia at Soldier Field on 17 June 1994.
